subject: Procurement & Pricing: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap & next steps — hosted vs dedicated vs private

Hi Alex — great to meet you and the Acme team this morning. Thanks for walking through your latency and compliance constraints. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our side: 

1) Summary of needs (what I heard)
- Production workloads: inference for customer-facing features, target p95 latency <150ms for 2k QPS bursts
- Data residency: EU for EU customers, US for US customers; some regulated data may need on-prem/Private deployment
- Procurement: prefers PO for enterprise deals; payment card only for pilots

2) Commercial path options to match procurement rules
- Hosted (on-demand): fastest onboarding, pay-as-you-go card or invoice for small pilots; not ideal if Acme requires monthly committed spend + PO
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): recommended if you want predictable throughput + single-tenant GPU pools; supports monthly/annual commits and invoiced PO terms
- Private (VPC/on-prem): for regulated data and air-gapped requirements; typical pricing is license + support and often requires longer procurement lead time

3) Information I need from you to scope pricing & packaging
- Expected committed token/embedding volumes (monthly) if considering Dedicated
- Procurement path: internal PO process timeline and any required contract language (SOW vs standard MSA)
- Marketplace interest: do you prefer to procure via cloud marketplace (AWS/GCP) or direct invoice?

Next steps: I'll draft a short commercial options matrix and SOW stub for your procurement team and loop in Aditya for contract/legal questions. Can you confirm whether Acme requires a PO for pilot beyond $10k/month? Also, Priya — is there an internal marketplace or GCP marketplace preference?

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — hosted vs dedicated vs private

Thanks Marissa — great session. A few clarifications from procurement/ops: 

- PO vs card: For pilots under $10k we can use a card. Anything beyond that generally needs a PO and our procurement team prefers annualized commitments for SaaS where possible.
- Marketplace: We have an internal preference for GCP Marketplace for easier billing consolidation; however procurement can accept direct invoices if there's a compelling reason.
- Contracting: Our legal team prefers to start with your standard MSA + SOW. We will surface any SOC2-related redlines early.

Volume guidance: For capacity planning, our first-phase pilot would be ~500k tokens/day (text gen + embeddings) and could scale to ~3M tokens/day within 6 months if performance looks good.

Next from us: Priya will coordinate procurement timeline and share an initial PO template. Are you able to provide a draft SOW and pricing tiers (hosted on-demand, dedicated 6/12-month commit, private deployment ballpark) by EOD Monday?

—Alex
VP Product, Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 07:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — hosted vs dedicated vs private

Thanks Alex — appreciate the clarity. Attaching the draft SOW and a pricing matrix with three rows (Hosted on-demand, Dedicated commit 6/12mo, Private one-time + annual support). Highlights in the matrix: 

- Hosted on-demand: no commit required; unit price per 1k tokens; good for proof-of-concept and low-risk pilots; supports marketplace via GCP if needed but billing may be consolidated differently (we can provide marketplace SKU).
- Dedicated (recommended if you want predictable latency/cost): reserved GPU pool with baseline commit — pricing tiers at 6-month and 12-month commits; supports PO invoicing and enterprise SLA. Includes option for burst capacity billed at lower unit price than hosted.
- Private: upfront deployment fee + annual support; longer procurement lead time and typical PO/license contract. Good when regulatory constraints require isolated control plane and KMS.

Questions for procurement: 
- PO timing: can Priya share an estimated date you can issue a PO if you choose Dedicated?
- Contract path: would Acme prefer Redwood's standard MSA + SOW or do you want to start from your draft?
- Marketplace: Priya, would GCP marketplace be preferred for the pilot (we can provision a marketplace SKU and separate billing), or would you rather have direct invoicing?

I've flagged a couple of common redlines in the attached SOW (data residency, audit logs, SLA credits). Aditya — can you validate the SLA language and whether we can support the residency split for EU/US within Dedicated? Lauren — can you confirm who on your side will own the MSA review if Acme sends their draft?

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_draft_v1.pdf, Redwood_pricing_matrix.xlsx

Best,
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — hosted vs dedicated vs private

Thanks all — quick technical/commercial notes: 

- Residency: Dedicated can be provisioned with region-specific pools; we can route EU traffic to an EU-dedicated pool to meet residency requirements. For strict on-prem Private, that remains a separate engagement.
- SLA & credits: We can accept the flagged SLA language with minor edits; I'll prepare suggested wording for the MSA.
- Procurement & billing: For pilots up to $10k/month, card is fine; for Dedicated we typically require a PO and monthly invoicing for committed spend. We can also publish a GCP Marketplace SKU to simplify procurement — note that marketplace takes time (~2-4 weeks for listing) but can speed future renewals.

Next steps (action items):
- Marissa: finalize the pricing matrix and SOW updates — include 6/12-month commit pricing and a short note on burst pricing. (owner: Marissa)
- Priya: share PO process & timeline + any internal PO template. (owner: Priya)
- Alex: confirm initial commit level you're comfortable with for Dedicated (if you want predictability).
- Aditya: draft MSA redline suggestions and validate SLA residency text.

Happy to jump on a quick call next week to walk procurement through the SOW if helpful.

Cheers,
Aditya
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
